en: first issue; launch of a publication

examples.ko: 이 잡지는 올해 창간 오십 주년을 맞았어요.
examples.en: This magazine marks the fiftieth anniversary of its launch this year.

examples.ko: 신문사는 창간 기념 행사를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The newspaper company is preparing an event to celebrate its founding.
The first issue sold out in a few days.

examples.ko: 그 잡지의 창간 멤버들이 오랜만에 모였어요.
examples.en: The founding members of the magazine got together for the first time in a long while.

examples.ko: 창간 때부터 이 칼럼을 읽어 왔어요.
examples.en: I have been reading this column since the very first issue.

examples.ko: 창간 준비 중인 웹진에서 글을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: A webzine that is getting ready to launch asked me to write something.

explain: 창간은 신문이나 잡지를 처음 낼 때 써요. 방송이 처음 시작할 때는 '개국', 가게는 '개업'처럼 분야마다 말이 달라요. 반대로 신문이나 잡지를 아예 접을 때는 '폐간'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This word is only for the very first issue of a newspaper or magazine. Other fields have their own words: a broadcaster starting up is '개국' and a shop opening is '개업'. Shutting a publication down for good is '폐간'.

en: launch (a newspaper or magazine); publish the first issue of

examples.en: A small publisher is launching a new literary magazine.

examples.ko: 그 신문은 백 년 전에 창간했어요.
examples.en: That newspaper was first published a hundred years ago.
I am going to start a newsletter with my friends.

examples.ko: 대학생들이 직접 잡지를 창간한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: Some university students once started a magazine on their own.

examples.ko: 잡지를 창간하고 나서 몇 달 동안 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: For several months after launching the magazine, I stayed up all night.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 자기 이름을 단 신문을 창간하려고 해요.
examples.en: That writer is trying to start a newspaper under his own name.

explain: 창간하다는 신문이나 잡지를 처음 펴낼 때만 써요. 책을 내는 것은 '출간하다', 이미 있는 잡지의 새 호를 내는 것은 '발간하다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 회사나 사람이 주어가 돼요.
explain_en: This verb is for bringing out the first issue of a newspaper or magazine. Publishing a book is '출간하다', and putting out a new issue of an existing magazine is '발간하다'. The subject is usually a company or a person.

examples.en: The soldiers divided the ammunition into boxes.
The ammunition was almost gone on the battlefield.
The warehouse is piled full of ammunition.
A truck loaded with ammunition drove past slowly.

examples.ko: 병사들이 남은 탄약을 하나씩 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: The soldiers counted the remaining ammunition one by one.

examples.ko: 탄약 보관소에는 아무나 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: Not just anyone can enter an ammunition depot.

explain: 탄약은 총알과 포탄을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 써요. 총알 하나는 '총알'이라고 해요. 군대 이야기나 뉴스에서 주로 나오고 '탄약이 떨어지다', '탄약을 보급하다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: This word covers bullets and shells together as a group. A single bullet is '총알'. It shows up in military talk and the news, in phrases like '탄약이 떨어지다' (run out of ammunition) and '탄약을 보급하다' (supply ammunition).

examples.en: The design of this bag is a bit tacky.

examples.ko: 후진 가게인 줄 알았는데 음식이 맛있었어요.
examples.en: I thought it was a shabby place, but the food was good.

examples.ko: 방이 너무 후져서 오래 못 있겠어요.
examples.en: The room is so shabby that I can't stay long.
I'm worried my outfit will look shabby.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 겉은 후지고 속은 깨끗해요.
examples.en: That restaurant looks shabby outside but is clean inside.

examples.ko: 어제 본 영화는 특수 효과가 정말 후졌어요.
examples.en: The special effects in the movie I saw yesterday were really lousy.

explain: '후지다'는 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 구어체예요. 어른이나 처음 만난 사람 앞에서는 '별로예요', '수준이 낮아요'처럼 부드럽게 말해요. 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례하게 들려요.
explain_en: '후지다' is casual spoken Korean for friends. With elders or people you've just met, soften it with '별로예요' (it's not great) or '수준이 낮아요' (the quality is low). Said directly about a person, it sounds rude.

examples.en: There is a good chance of rain tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이번 경기는 우리 팀이 이길 공산이 높아요.
examples.en: Our team is likely to win this game.

examples.ko: 그 계획이 성공할 공산은 크지 않아요.
examples.en: The chance that the plan succeeds is not high.

examples.ko: 값이 더 오를 공산이 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say prices could rise further.

examples.ko: 회의가 길어질 공산이 커서 점심을 미리 먹었어요.
examples.en: The meeting was likely to run long, so I ate lunch beforehand.

examples.ko: 늦게 출발하면 길이 막힐 공산이 많아요.
examples.en: If we leave late, the roads will probably be jammed.

explain: 공산은 '-ㄹ 공산이 크다/높다/많다/있다' 모양으로 써요. 앞일이 일어날 가능성을 말할 때 쓰고 '가능성'보다 뉴스나 글에서 딱딱하게 들려요. 같은 소리의 '공산당'과는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: This word is used in the pattern '-ㄹ 공산이 크다/높다/많다/있다' (it is likely that...). It sounds stiffer than '가능성' and fits the news and writing. It is a different word from the 공산 in '공산당' (communist party).

en: be disrupted; be disturbed; be thrown into disorder

examples.en: Train service was disrupted by the heavy snow.

examples.ko: 잦은 야근 때문에 생활 리듬이 교란되고 있어요.
examples.en: My daily rhythm is being thrown off by frequent overtime.

examples.ko: 강한 전파 때문에 신호가 교란될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Signals can be disrupted by strong radio waves.

examples.ko: 시장이 교란되면 물건값이 갑자기 오를 수 있어요.
examples.en: When the market is thrown into disorder, prices can suddenly rise.

examples.ko: 교란되어 있는 상태에서는 정확한 판단이 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to judge accurately when things are in disorder.

examples.ko: 시차 때문에 수면 패턴이 교란되는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Jet lag often disrupts sleep patterns.

explain: 교란되다는 원래 질서가 흐트러진 결과를 말할 때 써요. 뉴스, 경제, 과학 글에서 주로 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '엉망이 되다', '흐트러지다'가 더 자연스러워요. 일부러 흐트러뜨릴 때는 '교란하다'를 써요.
explain_en: This describes the result of an order being disturbed, and it appears mostly in the news, economics, and science writing. In daily talk, '엉망이 되다' or '흐트러지다' sounds more natural. When someone does it on purpose, use '교란하다'.

examples.en: A hacker is disrupting the server.
The enemy tried to jam the signal.
People who deliberately disrupt the market are punished.

examples.ko: 강한 빛이 동물의 눈을 교란할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Strong light can confuse an animal's eyes.

examples.ko: 가짜 뉴스가 사람들의 판단을 교란하고 있어요.
examples.en: Fake news is clouding people's judgment.
I was questioned on suspicion of obstructing the investigation.

explain: 교란하다는 일부러 어지럽힐 때, 교란되다는 어지러워진 결과를 말할 때 써요. 해킹, 시장, 수사 같은 뉴스 말투에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '방해하다', '어지럽히다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: '교란하다' is for disrupting something on purpose, while '교란되다' describes the disordered result. You will hear it in news talk about hacking, markets, and investigations. In everyday speech, '방해하다' (interfere) or '어지럽히다' (make a mess of) is more common.

en: be furnished with; be equipped with; be provided

examples.ko: 이 방에는 기본 가구가 모두 구비되어 있어요.
examples.en: This room is provided with all the basic furniture.
To apply, the documents have to be prepared first.
The hotel has been well equipped with the necessary facilities.

examples.ko: 응급 약품이 구비되어 있는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether emergency medicine is stocked.

examples.ko: 구비되는 장비가 많아서 따로 가져올 게 없어요.
examples.en: So much equipment is provided that there is nothing to bring.

examples.ko: 도서관에 새 컴퓨터가 구비되고 나서 이용자가 늘었어요.
examples.en: After new computers were installed in the library, more people started using it.

explain: 구비되다는 필요한 것이 이미 갖춰져 있을 때 써요. 숙소 안내나 공고문에서 '구비되어 있다' 모양이 가장 많아요. 말할 때는 '있어요', '갖춰져 있어요'가 더 편해요.
explain_en: This is used when what is needed is already in place. In lodging notices and announcements, the pattern '구비되어 있다' (is provided) is the most common. In speech, '있어요' or '갖춰져 있어요' is more relaxed.

en: furnish with; equip oneself with; have ready; provide

examples.en: I keep emergency medicine at home.
To apply, you need to prepare the documents below.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 손님용 우산을 구비하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our shop keeps umbrellas for customers.

examples.ko: 필요한 장비를 모두 구비한 뒤에 시작했어요.
examples.en: We started after getting all the necessary equipment ready.

examples.ko: 캠핑을 가기 전에 안전용품을 구비할 거예요.
examples.en: I will get safety gear before going camping.

examples.ko: 학교가 새 실험 도구를 구비하려고 예산을 늘렸어요.
examples.en: The school increased its budget to get new lab equipment.

explain: 구비하다는 필요한 물건이나 조건을 미리 갖춰 둔다는 느낌이라 '사다'보다 격식이 있어요. 안내문과 공고문에서 자주 보고, 대화에서는 '준비하다', '갖추다'를 많이 써요. '구비 서류'라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: This carries the feel of getting needed items or conditions ready in advance, so it is more formal than '사다' (buy). It appears in notices and announcements; in conversation people say '준비하다' or '갖추다'. There is also the term '구비 서류' (required documents).

examples.en: I have a stomach bug and have been throwing up all night.
I threw up from car sickness.

examples.ko: 아이가 열이 나고 구토하는 증상이 있어요.
examples.en: The child has a fever and is vomiting.
My stomach felt a little better after throwing up.

examples.ko: 상한 음식을 먹으면 구토할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Eating spoiled food can make you vomit.

examples.ko: 구토하면 물을 조금씩 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If you vomit, it is best to drink water in small sips.

explain: 구토하다는 병원이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 일상에서는 '토하다'가 가장 흔하고 '게우다'도 있어요. 속이 메스꺼운 느낌은 '울렁거리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: This is the formal term used in hospitals and the news. In daily life, '토하다' is the most common and '게우다' also exists. The queasy feeling before vomiting is '울렁거리다'.

examples.en: Many people avoid hard work.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 발표를 기피하려고 아픈 척했어요.
examples.en: That student pretended to be sick to get out of presenting.

examples.ko: 젊은 사람들이 시골 근무를 기피하는 경향이 있어요.
examples.en: Young people tend to shun working in the countryside.

examples.ko: 다들 청소 당번을 기피해서 제가 했어요.
examples.en: Everyone avoided cleaning duty, so I did it.
If you dodge responsibility, you lose trust.
It was a job so hard that everyone wanted to avoid it.

explain: 기피하다는 싫거나 부담스러워서 일부러 피할 때 써요. '피하다'는 비를 피하는 것처럼 눈에 보이는 상황에도 쓰지만, 기피하다는 일, 책임, 사람처럼 마음이 내키지 않는 대상에 써요. '병역 기피'처럼 굳은 말도 많아요.
explain_en: This is for deliberately steering clear of something you dislike or find burdensome. '피하다' also works for physical situations like dodging rain, but '기피하다' is for work, responsibility, or people you are reluctant about. It also appears in set phrases like '병역 기피' (draft evasion).

examples.ko: 도주 중인 범인을 경찰이 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are looking for the criminal on the run.
We confirmed the escape route on CCTV.
He did not succeed in escaping in the end.
He was detained because he was a flight risk.

examples.ko: 영화 속 도주 장면이 정말 아슬아슬했어요.
examples.en: The escape scene in the movie was really thrilling.
The person who helped with the escape was caught too.

explain: 도주는 범죄와 관련된 뉴스에서 많이 나오는 말이에요. 일상에서 도망가는 것은 '도망'이 더 흔하고, 가볍게는 '튀다'라고도 해요. '도주 차량', '도주 우려'가 자주 보이는 짝이에요.
explain_en: This word is common in crime news. In everyday talk, '도망' is more usual for running away, and the slangy '튀다' is also used. Frequent pairings are '도주 차량' (getaway vehicle) and '도주 우려' (flight risk).

en: literature and the arts; literary arts

examples.en: Our school has a literary club.
He graduated from the creative writing department.
I submitted a poem to a literary magazine.
I won a prize in this literary contest.

examples.ko: 문예 활동을 하면서 글쓰기 실력이 늘었어요.
examples.en: My writing improved while I was doing literary activities.

examples.ko: 문예 부흥기에는 훌륭한 작품이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many great works appeared during the Renaissance.

explain: 문예는 시, 소설, 수필처럼 글로 하는 예술을 주로 가리켜요. 그림과 음악까지 넓게 말할 때는 '예술'이나 '문화'를 써요. '문예부', '문예지', '문예 창작'처럼 다른 말과 붙어서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This mainly points to arts made with writing, such as poems, novels, and essays. For painting and music as well, use '예술' (art) or '문화' (culture). It often attaches to other words, as in '문예부' (literary club), '문예지' (literary magazine), and '문예 창작' (creative writing).

examples.en: They were persecuted because of their religion.
They kept their faith even through long persecution.
They left for another country to escape persecution.

examples.ko: 역사책에서 소수 민족에 대한 박해를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read about the persecution of minorities in a history book.
As the persecution grew worse, many people fled.
He fought on to the end against persecution.

explain: 박해는 힘 있는 쪽이 약한 쪽을 괴롭힐 때 쓰는 무거운 말이에요. 주로 종교, 민족, 역사 이야기에서 '박해를 받다', '박해에 시달리다'로 써요. 직장이나 학교의 괴롭힘에는 '괴롭힘'이 더 맞아요.
explain_en: This is a heavy word for the powerful oppressing the weak. It is mostly used in stories about religion, ethnic groups, and history, as in '박해를 받다' (be persecuted). For bullying at work or school, '괴롭힘' fits better.

examples.ko: 황제는 새 종교를 믿는 사람들을 박해했어요.
examples.en: The emperor persecuted people who believed in the new religion.
A society that persecutes minorities does not last long.
The king persecuted his officials, and the country fell into turmoil.

examples.ko: 누구도 다른 사람을 박해할 권리는 없어요.
examples.en: No one has the right to persecute others.

examples.ko: 과거에 학자들을 박해한 일이 부끄러운 역사로 남았어요.
examples.en: Persecuting scholars in the past remains a shameful part of history.

examples.ko: 자기와 다르다는 이유로 이웃을 박해하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not persecute your neighbors just because they are different from you.

explain: 박해하다는 주로 역사나 뉴스에서 힘 있는 쪽이 약한 쪽을 억누르는 상황에 써요. 학교나 회사에서 괴롭힐 때는 '괴롭히다'를 써요. 비슷한 말로 '핍박하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: This is used in history and news for the powerful pressing down on the weak. For bullying at school or work, use '괴롭히다'. A similar word is '핍박하다'.

en: be put on hold; be deferred

examples.en: That agenda item was put on hold at the meeting.

examples.ko: 예산 문제로 공사 계획이 보류되고 있어요.
examples.en: The construction plan is on hold because of budget issues.
The schedule slipped because the decision was put on hold.

examples.ko: 신청서가 보류되어 있는 이유를 알고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to know why my application is on hold.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 출발이 보류될 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If it rains a lot, the departure may be put on hold.
The project that had been put on hold will start again.

explain: 보류되다는 결정을 하지 않고 뒤로 남겨 둔다는 느낌이라 아예 없애는 '취소'와 달라요. 회의, 심사, 행정 장면에서 많이 나와요. '미뤄지다'는 날짜가 늦춰질 때, 보류되다는 판단 자체를 나중에 할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: This means a decision is left undecided for later, which is different from '취소' (cancellation), where it is dropped completely. It is common in meetings, screenings, and administration. '미뤄지다' fits when a date is pushed back, while '보류되다' fits when the judgment itself waits.

examples.en: The company put the launch of the new product on hold.

examples.ko: 일단 결정을 보류하고 더 생각해 볼게요.
examples.en: Let me hold off on deciding and think about it more.
The judges decided to withhold their judgment.

examples.ko: 급하지 않으면 구매를 보류하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: If it is not urgent, it is better to hold off on buying.
We will leave that issue pending until the next meeting.
I left without giving an answer.

explain: 보류하다는 결정이나 처리를 하지 않고 남겨 두는 것이라서 '취소하다'와 달리 나중에 다시 다룰 여지가 있어요. 공식적인 자리에서 '결정을 보류하다', '판단을 보류하다'로 자주 써요. 가볍게는 '미루다'를 써요.
explain_en: This means leaving a decision or action undone, so unlike '취소하다' (cancel), it can be taken up again later. In formal settings it appears as '결정을 보류하다' (hold off on a decision) or '판단을 보류하다' (withhold judgment). In casual speech, '미루다' (put off) is used.

en: occupy in advance; take first; secure ahead of others

examples.ko: 그 회사는 새 시장을 먼저 선점했어요.
examples.en: That company secured the new market first.
I went early to grab a good spot.
We have to secure the technology before our competitors do.

examples.ko: 빈 의자를 가방으로 선점하는 건 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: Claiming an empty seat with your bag is bad manners.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 도메인 이름을 선점하는 사람들이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people snap up popular domain names ahead of others.

examples.ko: 이 지역을 선점한 브랜드가 아직도 잘 팔려요.
examples.en: The brand that got into this area first still sells well.

explain: 선점하다는 자리, 시장, 기술처럼 남보다 앞서 차지하는 것에 써요. 시장 이야기에서는 긍정적이고, 자리를 맡아 두는 일에는 조금 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. '차지하다'보다 남보다 먼저라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: This is used for taking a spot, market, or technology ahead of others. In business talk it is positive, but for reserving seats it can carry a slightly critical tone. It stresses being first more strongly than '차지하다' (occupy).

examples.en: Our team scored the opening goal.
The government moved to respond ahead of time.
A preemptive attack is a risky choice.
A preventive test was done to stop the infection.
Thanks to the preemptive measures, the damage was reduced.

examples.ko: 문제가 커지기 전에 선제적으로 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: I told them in advance, before the problem grew.

explain: 선제는 혼자 쓰지 않고 '선제골', '선제 공격', '선제 대응'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 축구 중계에서는 '선제골'이, 뉴스에서는 '선제 조치'가 많이 나와요. 일이 생기기 전에 미리 움직인다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: This word is not used alone but attached to others, as in '선제골' (opening goal), '선제 공격' (preemptive strike), and '선제 대응' (preemptive response). Football commentary uses '선제골' a lot, and the news uses '선제 조치'. The feel is of moving before something happens.

examples.en: Economic dependence is growing steadily worse.

examples.ko: 한 회사에 대한 종속을 줄이려고 거래처를 늘렸어요.
examples.en: We added clients to reduce our dependence on a single company.
We learned about subordinate clauses in grammar class.

examples.ko: 하청 업체의 종속 구조가 문제라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the subordinate structure of subcontractors is a problem.
I worry about excessive dependence on machines.
Subordination and cooperation are completely different relationships.

explain: 종속은 힘이 약한 쪽이 강한 쪽에 매여 있는 상태에 써서 '독립'과 짝이에요. 경제나 정치 글, 문법 용어('종속절')에서 주로 봐요. 일상 말로는 '의존'이 부드럽지만, 종속은 스스로 결정하지 못한다는 점이 더 강해요.
explain_en: This describes a weaker side being tied to a stronger one, and it pairs with '독립' (independence). You see it in economics and politics writing and in grammar terms like '종속절' (subordinate clause). '의존' (reliance) is milder; '종속' stresses the inability to decide for yourself.

en: be subordinate to; be subordinated to; be dependent on

examples.ko: 그 나라 경제는 한 나라에 종속되어 있어요.
examples.en: That country's economy is dependent on a single country.

examples.ko: 작은 회사가 큰 회사에 종속되기 쉬워요.
examples.en: Small companies easily end up subordinate to big ones.

examples.ko: 예술이 돈에 종속되면 안 된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think art should not be subordinated to money.

examples.ko: 한 사람의 의견에 종속되지 않도록 팀 회의를 열었어요.
examples.en: We held a team meeting so that we would not be subject to one person's opinion.
Once you become dependent, it is hard to get out.

examples.ko: 한 회사에 종속되었던 작은 업체가 마침내 독립했어요.
examples.en: The small firm that had been subordinate to one company finally became independent.

explain: 종속되다는 어떤 힘에 매여 스스로 결정하지 못하는 상태에 써요. '독립하다'와 반대 방향이에요. 사람, 회사, 나라 모두 주어가 될 수 있고, 묶여 있는 대상은 '에'로 나타내요. 예를 들면 '돈에 종속되다'예요.
explain_en: This is used when something is bound to a power and cannot decide for itself, the opposite direction of '독립하다' (become independent). People, companies, and countries can all be the subject, and the thing they are tied to takes '에', as in '돈에 종속되다' (be enslaved to money).

en: end of a TV series' run; finale

examples.en: Fans were sad at the news that the drama was ending.
With the end of the run near, I am looking forward to the last episode.

examples.ko: 종영 후에도 그 배우는 계속 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The actor stayed popular even after the show ended.
An early end to the show was decided because of low ratings.
The actors cried at the wrap party.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 사랑받은 예능 프로그램이 종영을 알렸어요.
examples.en: The long-loved variety show announced that it was ending.

explain: 종영은 드라마, 예능, 라디오처럼 정해진 방송이 끝날 때 써요. 영화는 '상영 종료', 공연은 '폐막'처럼 분야마다 달라요. 시작할 때는 '첫방', '방영 시작'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This is for the end of a scheduled broadcast such as a drama, variety show, or radio program. Other fields differ: a film's run is '상영 종료' and a performance is '폐막'. The start of a show is '첫방' or '방영 시작'.

en: be supported; be held up; be sustained

examples.ko: 이 다리는 굵은 기둥들로 지탱되고 있어요.
examples.en: This bridge is held up by thick pillars.
Relationships sustained by trust last long.
There was a time when the economy was propped up by exports.
The building is old and barely holding up.
That village has been kept going by tourism.

examples.ko: 기둥 하나에 지탱되는 구조가 불안해 보여요.
examples.en: A structure held up by a single pillar looks unstable.

explain: 지탱되다는 무너지지 않고 버티는 것을 받쳐 주는 무엇이 있을 때 써요. 건물 같은 물건뿐 아니라 경제나 관계처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에도 써요. 스스로 버티는 것은 '버티다'를 써요.
explain_en: This is used when something stays up because something else is supporting it. It works for objects like buildings and also for invisible things like an economy or a relationship. When something holds out on its own, use '버티다'.

examples.en: Pillars hold up the roof.
He supported himself by leaning on a cane.
It is hard to keep going without medicine.

examples.ko: 이 선반은 무거운 책을 지탱할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This shelf can support heavy books.
My family's support kept me going.

examples.ko: 작은 가게들이 이 동네 경제를 지탱하고 있어요.
examples.en: Small shops are propping up this neighborhood's economy.

explain: 지탱하다는 받쳐서 무너지지 않게 하거나, 어려운 상황을 버티게 할 때 써요. '버티다'는 자기가 힘든 일을 견딜 때 쓰고, 지탱하다는 물건이나 사람, 마음이 다른 것을 받쳐 주는 느낌이에요. '지탱해 주다'로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: This is for holding something up so it does not collapse, or for helping something get through hard times. '버티다' is for enduring hardship yourself, while '지탱하다' feels like an object, person, or feeling bearing the load for something else. It is often used as '지탱해 주다'.

examples.en: This accident is the result of failure across the board.

examples.ko: 총체적 난국이라는 말이 딱 맞는 상황이에요.
examples.en: 'A total mess' is exactly the right phrase for this situation.
We need to look at the problem as a whole.

examples.ko: 그 책은 한국 사회의 총체를 보여 주려고 했어요.
examples.en: That book tried to show the whole picture of Korean society.

examples.ko: 교육은 사람의 총체적 성장을 도와야 해요.
examples.en: Education should help a person's overall growth.

examples.ko: 한 가지가 아니라 총체적 점검이 필요해요.
examples.en: A comprehensive check is needed, not just one thing.

explain: 총체는 '총체적', '총체적으로'처럼 뒤에 붙여 전체를 아울러 볼 때 많이 써요. '전체'보다 글 느낌이 강하고, 뉴스에서 '총체적 부실', '총체적 난국'이 자주 나와요. 부분만 볼 때는 '부분적'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used with endings, as in '총체적' and '총체적으로', for looking at everything together. It feels more written than '전체' (whole), and the news often uses '총체적 부실' (failure across the board) and '총체적 난국' (a total mess). Looking at only part of something is '부분적'.

en: expel; drive out; remove or withdraw (from a market or position)

examples.en: The company ousted the employee who had problems.

examples.ko: 협회는 규칙을 어긴 선수를 퇴출하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The association decided to expel the player who broke the rules.
Dangerous products must be pulled from the market.

examples.ko: 플랫폼이 거짓 정보를 올린 계정을 퇴출했어요.
examples.en: The platform removed the account that posted false information.

examples.ko: 주식 시장은 기준에 못 미친 기업을 퇴출해요.
examples.en: The stock market delists companies that fall short of the standard.

examples.ko: 나쁜 관행을 퇴출하려면 모두가 노력해야 해요.
examples.en: To drive out bad practices, everyone has to make an effort.

explain: 퇴출하다는 조직, 시장, 자리에서 내보낸다는 느낌이라 '해고하다'보다 범위가 넓어요. 직원뿐 아니라 선수, 기업, 제품, 계정에도 써요. 일상 대화보다 뉴스에서 많이 보고, 당하는 쪽에서는 '퇴출되다', '퇴출당하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: This means pushing something out of an organization, market, or position, so it is broader than '해고하다' (fire). It applies to players, companies, products, and accounts as well as employees. You see it more in the news than in conversation, and from the receiving side it is '퇴출되다' or '퇴출당하다'.

examples.en: The child suddenly plopped down.

examples.ko: 한 달 사이에 월급이 팍 깎였어요.
examples.en: Within a month, my pay was slashed sharply.
I jammed the wooden stick into the ground.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣자마자 기분이 팍 상했어요.
examples.en: My mood soured the moment I heard that.
I smacked the button and the machine turned off.
The temperature dropped sharply compared to yesterday.

explain: 팍은 동작이나 변화가 갑자기, 힘차게 일어날 때 쓰는 흉내말이에요. '팍 줄다', '팍 쓰러지다'처럼 변화가 크고 빠를 때 어울려요. 비슷한 '확'은 크게 달라질 때, '푹'은 깊이 빠질 때 써요. 편한 말투라 공식 글에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: This sound-imitating word marks an action or change that happens suddenly and with force, as in '팍 줄다' (shrink sharply) and '팍 쓰러지다' (collapse). The similar '확' is for a big sudden change, and '푹' is for sinking deep. It is casual, so it rarely appears in formal writing.

examples.en: The anger came out directly in the way of speaking.
His dissatisfaction started to come out in his actions.
The way emotions come out differs from person to person.

examples.ko: 억눌린 스트레스가 갑자기 표출될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Pent-up stress can suddenly burst out.
The artist's loneliness comes through in the painting.

examples.ko: 분노가 거칠게 표출되는 것을 보고 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised to see the anger erupt so roughly.

explain: 표출되다는 마음속에 있던 감정이나 생각이 겉으로 드러날 때 써요. 화, 불만, 스트레스처럼 쌓였던 감정과 잘 어울려요. 사람이 의도해서 말할 때는 '표현하다', 저절로 드러날 때는 '나타나다'를 많이 써요.
explain_en: This is used when feelings or thoughts held inside come out into the open. It goes well with built-up feelings such as anger, discontent, and stress. When a person says it on purpose, '표현하다' (express) is common, and for something showing by itself, '나타나다' (appear).

examples.en: Lots of fish are caught in this stretch of sea.
A warning was issued for the waters as the typhoon approached.
The ships went around the dangerous waters.
A drill is being held in the waters near our country.
The water temperature differs from one sea area to another.
The rescue team arrived at the accident site at sea.

explain: 해역은 뉴스나 일기예보에서 '인근 해역', '사고 해역'처럼 바다의 한 구역을 가리킬 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '바다'라고 해요. 강이나 호수 같은 곳은 '수역'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In the news and weather forecasts, this points to one area of the sea, as in '인근 해역' (nearby waters) and '사고 해역' (accident site at sea). In daily conversation people just say '바다' (sea). For rivers and lakes, the word is '수역'.

en: be returned; be restored; be reduced to

examples.en: The profits were returned to the employees.
The donations are being given back to the local community.

examples.ko: 모든 문제가 돈으로 환원되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Not every problem can be reduced to money.
It takes time to be restored to the original state.
The system was changed so that taxes are returned to citizens.
They promised that the earnings would go back to society.

explain: 환원되다는 가져간 것이 다시 돌아가거나, 복잡한 것이 하나로 줄어들 때 써요. 이익, 세금, 기부처럼 돈이 사회로 돌아갈 때 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '돌아가다'가 쉬워요.
explain_en: This is used when something taken goes back, or when something complex is boiled down to one thing. It is common for profits, taxes, and donations flowing back to society. In everyday speech, '돌아가다' (go back) is easier.

en: give back; return; restore; reduce to

examples.en: The company gives its profits back to society.

examples.ko: 그 부자는 재산을 사회에 환원하기로 했어요.
examples.en: That rich man decided to give his wealth back to society.
I want to give back the help I received to my neighbors.

examples.ko: 복잡한 문제를 하나의 원인으로 환원하면 오해가 생겨요.
examples.en: Reducing a complicated problem to a single cause leads to misunderstanding.
Iron is obtained by reducing iron oxide.
A part of the earnings was given back to the fans.

explain: 환원하다는 얻은 이익이나 도움을 다시 돌려줄 때 '사회에 환원하다'로 가장 많이 써요. '돌려주다'보다 격식이 있고 기부, 나눔의 느낌이 있어요. 과학 시간에는 산소를 떼어 내는 반응을 '환원하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its most common use is '사회에 환원하다', giving back gains or help you received. It is more formal than '돌려주다' (return) and carries a sense of donation and sharing. In science class, it also names the reaction that removes oxygen from a substance.
